title: ShelfKit's rules
description: The boundaries every change to ShelfKit keeps.

sections.heading: The crates are the product
sections.body: crates/ compiles native for the CLI and to WASM for the Worker and the browser, so they cannot disagree. Keep it free of Cloudflare, network, and async-runtime dependencies.

sections.heading: APM owns install
sections.body: `shelfkit compile` writes apm.yml and stops. It never writes a lockfile, never materializes skills into harness directories, and never runs APM unless `install` was asked for. Never parse human-oriented apm output.

sections.heading: The registry is one library
sections.body: crates/registry decides every rule; a host does I/O and nothing else. A new rule goes into the library with a case in conformance/cases.json, which both hosts run.

sections.heading: Storage
sections.body: One Durable Object per shelf, with its own SQLite. No D1 and no cross-shelf query. Content lives in R2 keyed by sha256; databases hold metadata only.

sections.heading: Keys
sections.body: One auth module turns a Bearer key, HTTP Basic, or the browser's cookie into a session. Nothing caches a key's resolution, and a key is never printed or logged.
